Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Med iCorp's security reviewers asked for a clearer mapping of how Redwood handles:

- BYOK in on-prem / VPC installs (supported KMS/HSM patterns, escrow options)
- Which subprocessors would have any access in a private deployment (esp. during hardware maintenance)
- Network/egress controls & how logs/telemetry are handled across US/EU boundaries

We're preparing legal review and want to avoid ambiguous DPA language. Specifically, can you confirm:
1) Whether operator access is ever permitted into the customer VPC or on-prem environment (and under what conditions)
2) Whether telemetry/health metrics transmitted back to Redwood contain any customer plaintext or only anonymous metadata
3) What notice you provide before onboarding a new subprocessor for private deployments, and whether you will carve out any subprocessors entirely from on-prem installs

If you can attach a short DPA excerpt (byok + subprocessors clause) and an ops matrix, that will speed our review.

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then details + attachments.

Short answers:
1) Operator access: Not by default. For hosted Redwood we have standard operator access to the control plane; for Private (VPC / on-prem) operator access is limited to the control plane components you opt into. For fully air-gapped on-prem installs Redwood personnel do not have network access unless a customer-approved breakglass is enacted (documented, time-limited, auditable).

2) Telemetry: We transmit only non-content telemetry by default. That includes anonymized resource metrics, kernel-level performance traces (no model inputs/outputs or customer PII). If you choose to enable additional diagnostics we can restrict fields and redact at source.

3) Subprocessors: For Private deployments we limit subprocessors to cloud infra partners and hardware vendors; personnel-facing subprocessors (e.g., on-site maintenance vendors) can be excluded by contract. We provide 30 days' notice before any new subprocessor and will provide a subprocessor questionnaire/attestation for hardware vendors.

Attached: a short DPA excerpt focusing on BYOK and subprocessors, plus an operator-access matrix. Key items in the excerpt:
- BYOK modes supported: KMS customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK), HSM-backed PKCS#11 integrations for on-prem HSMs, and an escrow workflow for legal hold where keys can be sealed to a neutral escrow with customer approval.
- Operator access carveouts: operator breakglass requires dual approval (customer security lead + Redwood security), full audit trails, and a prescriptive runbook limited to specific time windows.
- Subprocessor control: subprocessors are permitted only where absolutely necessary (e.g., hardware swap). Customers may require Redwood to use customer-approved on-site vendors or require vendor background checks and a limited-latency maintenance window.

I'll loop in Karthik and Marcus to add technical specifics on telemetry and the maintenance workflow.

Regards,

Tom / Naomi — adding the technical breakdown you asked for. Summary first, details after.

Summary:
- Operator network access into customer VPC/on-prem: only via customer-initiated tunnel or jump host that you control; Redwood operators never receive direct credentials unless the customer explicitly provides short-lived access tokens or a VPN session, and then only after approval.
- Telemetry payloads: default telemetry contains only aggregated CPU/GPU utilization, disk I/O metrics, queue latency percentiles, and bounded anonymized error codes. No model inputs/outputs or request payloads are transmitted.
- Maintenance subprocessors: typical subprocessors are hardware OEMs (e.g., Cisco/Lenovo), and a small set of managed-service vendors for physical rack support. For on-prem we can require customer-approved vendors or have you supply local staff to perform swaps.

Technical details:
- Breakglass flow: customer raises ticket with authorization token; Redwood responds with time-limited signed session (max 4 hours), an operator-only account is created with mfa and has actions logged to an immutable audit sink. We ship logs to a customer-controlled SIEM endpoint if desired (TLS + mutual auth).
- Telemetry redaction: we run a pre-publish filter that strips any ASCII-like chunks above a threshold length (prevents accidental exfil of text blobs) and enforce schema validation on every metric.
- Key escrow / recovery: we support an escrow policy where CMKs are wrapped with a customer KMS key and a secondary escrow key held in a hardware escrow (signed attestation required for release). This can be extended to a multi-party escrow if required for your legal hold process.
- Subprocessor notice: Redwood provides a 30-day notification by email + a maintained subprocessor registry with attestations (SOC2/ISO/contract points). For private installs we will exclude any subprocessor that cannot provide an on-site background check or refuses to sign a limited-scope SOW.

Marcus can add retention numbers and audit-residency details. Happy to schedule a short call with your security team to walk the flow diagrams.

- Karthik
Senior Systems Architect
Redwood Inference
